metadata.note: The Rutland Railroad's Green Mountain Flyer, the historical predecessor of Amtrak's Ethan Allen Express through western Vermont. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Green Mountain Flyer, Rutland Railroad), american-rails.com
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

properties.speed_source: estimated/blended across the line's history; unsourced

segments.note: The Green Mountain Flyer, begun in 1892, was the Rutland Railroad's best-known train, running New York-Rutland-Burlington and on to Montreal via Canadian National at Rouses Point, with a broiler-buffet-parlor car and a Troy-New York diner in its peak years. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
sources: Segment-level: this segment's own note carries the citation for its dates and service. Supporting references for the line:
Wikipedia (Green Mountain Flyer, Rutland Railroad), american-rails.com

segments.note: Postwar competition from cars, paved roads and trucking eroded Rutland's passenger, milk, mail and express income; the Flyer was cut back to originate at Burlington rather than Montreal, and was discontinued in 1953 as the Rutland ended all passenger service. Amtrak's Ethan Allen Express revived New York-Rutland service in 1996 and reached Burlington in 2022 - see amtrak.geojson. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
